metadata.title: Rule-Based Astrochemical Knowledge System
notes: Manual astrochemical rules are educational qualitative rules.
NASA rules classify only broad environmental regimes from archive parameters.
No NASA rule claims that a molecule definitely exists.

rules.title: Cold dense grain-surface regime
rules.explanation: Cold, dense conditions with dust are compatible with an environment where adsorption and grain-surface chemistry can be important.
rules.source_note: Educational qualitative rule; thresholds are project bins and should not be treated as universal physical boundaries.

rules.title: Freeze-out is plausible
rules.explanation: Cold grain-surface conditions make adsorption/freeze-out of some gas-phase species plausible.

rules.title: CO surface hydrogenation pathway
rules.explanation: If CO is present on cold grain surfaces, successive hydrogen-addition chemistry becomes a plausible pathway.
rules.source_note: Qualitative starter rule; final research use would require literature-calibrated physical conditions.

rules.title: Methanol ice formation is plausible
rules.explanation: CO hydrogenation on grains provides a known qualitative pathway toward methanol ice; this is a plausibility inference, not an abundance prediction.

rules.title: Warm grain desorption regime
rules.explanation: Warmer dust can release some icy material to the gas phase; exact desorption temperatures are species-dependent.
rules.source_note: 100 K is an educational warm-region project threshold, not a universal desorption temperature.

rules.title: UV-driven chemistry
rules.explanation: A strong ultraviolet field can make photodissociation and photochemical processing important.

rules.title: Cosmic-ray ionization chemistry
rules.explanation: Cosmic-ray ionization can initiate ion-molecule reaction chains in dense, shielded gas.

rules.title: Cold dense shielded profile
rules.explanation: The selected project-level conditions resemble a cold, dense, UV-shielded environment.
rules.source_note: Project profile, not a formal astronomical classification standard.

rules.title: Warm dense profile
rules.explanation: The selected project-level conditions resemble a warm, dense environment.
rules.source_note: Project profile, not a formal astronomical classification standard.

rules.title: Cool equilibrium-temperature bin
rules.explanation: For this PBL, equilibrium temperatures below 250 K are grouped into a simple 'cool' demonstration bin.
rules.source_note: Project bin for explainable reasoning; not a formal universal exoplanet taxonomy.

rules.title: Moderate equilibrium-temperature bin
rules.explanation: For this PBL, 250-500 K is treated as a moderate equilibrium-temperature demonstration bin.
rules.source_note: Project bin; does not imply habitability.

rules.title: Hot equilibrium-temperature bin
rules.explanation: For this PBL, equilibrium temperatures at or above 1000 K are grouped into a 'hot' demonstration bin.
rules.source_note: Project bin for transparent rule-based reasoning.

rules.title: Near-Earth-size radius bin
rules.explanation: The recorded radius falls in this PBL's small-planet demonstration bin.
rules.source_note: Project bin, not a definitive composition classification.

rules.title: Intermediate-size radius bin
rules.explanation: The recorded radius falls in this PBL's intermediate-size demonstration bin.
rules.source_note: Project bin; radius alone does not determine composition.

rules.title: Giant-size radius bin
rules.explanation: The recorded radius falls in this PBL's giant-planet demonstration bin.
rules.source_note: Project bin used for transparent rule chaining.

rules.title: Cool small-planet environmental profile
rules.explanation: The available archive parameters are compatible with a cool, near-Earth-size bulk environment.
rules.source_note: This does not establish atmospheric composition or habitability.

rules.title: Moderate intermediate-size environmental profile
rules.explanation: The archive values are compatible with a moderate-temperature, intermediate-size bulk environment.
rules.source_note: Bulk properties alone do not determine molecules.

rules.title: Hot giant environmental profile
rules.explanation: The archive values are compatible with a hot giant-planet bulk environment.

rules.title: Composition requires spectroscopy
rules.explanation: Equilibrium temperature and bulk radius can describe an environment, but they do not prove which molecules are present.
rules.source_note: Scientific safeguard used by V1 to avoid overclaiming.
